profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the modeling lead and the applied research engineering lead on an internal ML research project that applies dichotomous Item Response Theory to application deployment controls and SRE outcomes. The team is preparing a pilot readout for the platform architecture review next week, using historical production deployment data to estimate an Application Deployment Score, item-level difficulty/discrimination for deployment controls, and a soft error-budget adjustment signal for interdependent services. The agenda is to align on the modeling input handoff, the frozen data snapshot to use, what counts as a deployment record in the shared dataset, and what each person will deliver before the review. The expected outcome is an apparent agreement on interfaces, deadlines, artifact locations, and readiness criteria for the pilot package.

members.name: Dr. Anika Rao
members.expertise: Bayesian modeling, psychometrics, reliability metrics, applied ML research
members.background: Anika joined the ML research group after doing academic work on latent-variable models and has recently been translating educational measurement methods into software reliability and DevOps analytics.
members.private_state: She wants a methodologically clean pilot that can support a publishable internal research memo, and she is worried that operational data noise and inconsistent release records will make the IRT estimates look unstable.
hidden_assumptions: A 'deployment' is a distinct customer-exposed rollout event after a canary is promoted, even if multiple rollout waves belong to the same artifact version.
The canonical outcome labels are the manually adjudicated incident-review sheet used in prior reliability analyses, because it reflects final human attribution rather than raw warehouse state.
Freezing the dataset means freezing the row set and schema for modeling; late corrections to outcome labels are still acceptable if they improve attribution quality.
A 'pilot-ready' result means posterior scores, item parameter tables, and a few convincing trend plots for representative services, even if the workflow is still partly notebook-driven.

members.name: Leo Martinez
members.expertise: ML data pipelines, analytics infrastructure, SRE telemetry integration, reproducible experimentation
members.background: Leo previously worked on reliability analytics inside a platform engineering team and now supports research projects by turning messy operational signals into versioned datasets and repeatable pipelines.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid bespoke manual data handling that will become his team's maintenance burden later, and he is trying to ensure that anything shown in the review can be rerun automatically from warehouse assets.
hidden_assumptions: A 'deployment' is the shipped artifact version or release identifier, with regional waves and canary stages collapsed into one record for that version.
The canonical labels are whatever is in the versioned warehouse table `slo_breach_labels`, because only auditable, scheduled assets should feed a research pipeline.
Freezing the dataset means creating an immutable snapshot table that will not change afterward, including no label backfills or attribution edits.
A 'pilot-ready' package means an end-to-end automated run for all tier-1 services with outputs published to the shared dashboard and reproducible from code only.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both casually agree to compute the Application Deployment Score 'per deployment.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means each customer-visible rollout event, so a single artifact version may appear multiple times if it rolled out in separate waves or regions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means one record per shipped artifact version, with canary and regional rollout stages consolidated.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In reliability discussions, 'deployment' and 'release' are often used interchangeably, and both interpretations sound normal enough that neither person expects the term itself to need unpacking.

misalignment_points.topic: Which historical snapshot is the baseline
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to using 'the Q2 snapshot' or 'last quarter's snapshot' for the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the manually curated export assembled at the end of Q2 for the previous reliability study, which includes adjudicated incident attributions and some hand-fixed deployment-control fields.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the warehouse snapshot table materialized in early Q3 from scheduled pipelines, which includes late-arriving telemetry but no manual corrections.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There really is a commonly referenced 'Q2 snapshot' in team conversations, but two nearby artifacts inherited that name in different contexts, so the phrase creates false shared reference.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'freeze the dataset' permits after handoff
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'freeze the dataset by Thursday' before modeling and review prep.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes the freeze is about stabilizing the modeling matrix shape; if an SLO breach gets re-attributed before the review, she still expects the label to be corrected in place.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes a freeze means the snapshot becomes immutable once published, because reproducibility and lineage require no post-freeze edits.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are following legitimate professional norms attached to the phrase 'freeze the dataset,' and in a coordination meeting it sounds like simple schedule alignment rather than a rule that needs explicit scope.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they want the work to be 'pilot-ready' for next week's architecture review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the research story is ready if the scores and item-level patterns look coherent on a few representative services and can support the conceptual argument.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the deliverable is ready only if the full pipeline runs across all tier-1 services and the outputs are published in the standard dashboard location.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The review is framed as a pilot rather than a launch, so each person reasonably defaults to their own discipline's readiness bar without feeling a need to negotiate it explicitly.
